newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close lower, above limit losses.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close lower, above limit losses.

text.p: CME lumber futures recovered from a limit loss of $10.00 per thousand board feet but ended lower, with values overall dragged down by falling cash lumber prices, traders said.
Lumber closed $8.20 to $0.20 per tbf lower with limitless July off most at $372.00 per tbf and September off $6.80 at $367.20 after being limit down at $364.00 earlier.

Futures were under pressure from the start from tumbling cash lumber. Long liquidation and new selling pushed September down throught the 40-day average to touch off stops. Short covering pared losses at the close, traders said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $364 per tbf, $8 lower than last Friday and down $11 from a week ago.
Some mills sold wood as low as $360 or slightly lower as increased offerings in the secondary market put pressure on the entire cash market, traders added.
Saul Stone bought September late. ABN Chicogo Corp spread long September/short July early. ING bought on the scale down early, pit sources said.
